subject: gk
question: The Geological Survey of India (GSI) was established in 1851 primarily to explore coal reserves for ________.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Railway**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Geological Survey of India (GSI)** was established in **1851**, primarily for the purpose of exploring and studying the **coal reserves** in India.
 
• The primary motivation for the establishment of GSI was the growing need for coal to support the development of **railways in India**.
 
• During the mid-19th century, the **railway network** in India was expanding rapidly under British colonial rule.
 
• **Coal** was a crucial source of fuel to power the **steam locomotives** used in railways during this period.
 
• GSI's role included **surveying and mapping the coal reserves** to ensure the availability of sufficient resources for railway operations.
 
• The establishment of GSI marked a significant step in the development of the **industrial sector** in India, as coal mining and railway expansion were interlinked.
 
• Over time, GSI expanded its scope to include other areas of geological research and exploration, but its initial focus on coal exploration was pivotal for the progress of India's **railway infrastructure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Export to Japan**__

 __
 
• India has historically exported several commodities to **Japan**, including minerals and textiles, but coal was not a significant export to Japan during the mid-19th century.
 
• Japan's industrialization began later in the 19th century, and its dependence on imported coal was relatively low compared to other nations during that time.
 
 
 
• **Sea Transport**__
 __
 
• Coal was not primarily explored for sea transport in India during the 19th century.
 
• While coal was used in ships, the focus in India at that time was primarily on utilizing coal for **railways and industrial purposes**.
 
 
 
• **Textile Mill**__
 
 
• Textile mills do require energy, but during the mid-19th century in India, the primary focus of coal exploration was to support railway development rather than textile production.
 
• Textile mills in India started gaining prominence later, especially during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
